history.title: Rate-schedule threshold gate

style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: On a brushed steel workbench in a data hall, a modular pricing-schedule bay sits off-center left. Two vertical aluminum rails hold rectangular plug-in pricing modules; all modules below a horizontal steel threshold beam are graphite with milled latch tabs, and all above are oxidized copper. A slim token-length rail with a sliding stop rises from below and crosses the beam just past the line. An unlatched safety-yellow inspection gate marks the threshold. One hard key light from upper left rakes across graphite, copper and safety yellow, throwing long contact shadows; 85mm macro, shallow depth of field, fine film grain; extreme asymmetry, no lettering, no people.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random letters, numbers, watermarks, legible labels, screen UI, logos
rationale: The article is a single rule, gate, and price-shift story with no physical facility to photograph, so component_assembly lets the rate schedule itself become a legible mechanical threshold: a lower standard column flips to a higher long-context column at a physical line, with the token rail crossing just past it.
cue: crossing a schedule's line reprices every token in the request
subject: A modular pricing-schedule bay with two vertical rails, graphite standard-context modules below a threshold beam, copper long-context modules above, and a token-length rail crossing just past the line.
core_thesis: Context length is a price column, not a capability: crossing a schedule's line reprices every token in the request, so the 95th-percentile prompt length sets what a workflow costs.
core_conflict: The standard-rate column under the declared context line collides with the dearer long-context column above it; one token can move the entire request into the premium schedule, so the long tail of p95 prompts decides cost.
composition: Extreme asymmetry with the assembly off-center left, horizontal threshold beam splitting the frame, and a long cast shadow to the right.

title: Your 200K Prompt'S Hidden Rate Cliff

review.depicts: A metal workbench holding a cluster of machined metal chassis boxes on the left, a thin vertical metal rail with a small sliding clamp rising through the middle, a horizontal beam-like shelf behind it, four green-patinated copper plates standing along the top shelf, and a yellow-framed open metal box on the right, lit by a lamp against a dark rack-filled background.
review.reason: It builds the ordered modular bay with a vertical rail and modules divided above and below a horizontal beam, which reads as the article's length-threshold pricing-schedule mechanism rather than a foreign scene, though the two-tier copper/standard pricing split is only loosely legible.

input.prompt:
On a brushed steel workbench in a data hall, a modular pricing-schedule bay sits off-center left. Two vertical aluminum rails hold rectangular plug-in pricing modules; all modules below a horizontal steel threshold beam are graphite with milled latch tabs, and all above are oxidized copper. A slim token-length rail with a sliding stop rises from below and crosses the beam just past the line. An unlatched safety-yellow inspection gate marks the threshold. One hard key light from upper left rakes across graphite, copper and safety yellow, throwing long contact shadows; 85mm macro, shallow depth of field, fine film grain; extreme asymmetry, no lettering, no people.

Do not include: people, faces, hands, garbled text, random lettering, numbers, signage, watermarks, UI, logos.
